The library was nearly empty when the last class ended. On the second floor of the old brick building where the study hall had stood decades ago in 1919—when the entire faculty was still huddled in a cramped space in the attic waiting for a government inspector to actually show up—there was a solitary oak desk placed under a window that overlooked the city street.
